title: India seeks Nepal's airspace for Bagdogra flights in exchange for Bhairahawa route
dek: Kathmandu is ready to accept the north Bengal request but wants more time on a second one near Raxaul, reports say, ahead of Prime Minister Balendra Shah's expected visit to New Delhi.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India has asked Nepal to let international flights to and from Bagdogra airport in north Bengal use eastern Nepali airspace, offering in return the extra air entry route to Bhairahawa in western Nepal that Kathmandu has sought for more than a decade, according to reports from both capitals. Nepali officials say they are prepared to accept the Bagdogra request but need more time to study a second Indian request, for airspace near Raxaul on the Bihar border.

The proposal was put to a Nepali delegation led by Mukesh Dangol, director general of the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN), at talks with Indian aviation regulators in New Delhi last week, the reports said. Two officials said India wanted both arrangements concluded as a single package. Nepali officials said they had not expected the counter-proposal. "We have told them that we need some time to study the Raxaul proposal," one senior official said, according to one report.

## Why Nepal wants the route

Nearly all international flights into Nepal now enter its airspace through a single point, Simara, south of Kathmandu, about 90 per cent of them according to reports. Nepal has asked for years for more entry points through Nepalgunj and Mahendranagar in the west and Biratnagar and Janakpur in the east, so that its two new international airports can attract airlines.

Neither is doing well. Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa, near the Indian border, has no regular international flights, only charters. Pokhara International Airport has one regular international service, a daily Flydubai flight that began in September; attempts at regular flights to Chinese cities did not last, and no commercial flights from India have started, according to reports. Nepal has also asked India to lower the minimum altitude for aircraft using the existing western entry via Mahendranagar from 39,000 feet to 35,000 feet, since most airliners cruise between 29,000 and 35,000 feet.

The issue has come up at almost every top-level meeting since 2011. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 2014 visit to Kathmandu the two sides set a six-month deadline that was missed, and in 2016 India gave in-principle consent to more entry points that was never put into effect, according to reports. India has cited airspace security and the need for technical studies. Indian officials have refused routes at lower altitudes near military airbases such as Gorakhpur, one report said, citing an unnamed Nepali official.

## The China question

Pokhara airport was built by a Chinese company with a loan of about $216 million from China's Export-Import Bank, and a Chinese contractor also worked on Bhairahawa, which was financed by Nepal's government, the Asian Development Bank and the OPEC Fund, according to reports. Some Nepali analysts link India's reluctance to the Chinese role. "Chinese involvement may be the reason behind the denial of air routes," the geopolitical analyst Ajay Bhadra Khanal said, according to one report. India has never given that as a reason.

## What it means for north Bengal

Bagdogra, near Siliguri, is a civil enclave inside an Indian Air Force station and the main airport for north Bengal, Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills. It sits in the Siliguri Corridor, the narrow strip of land that joins north-eastern India to the rest of the country. India has not said publicly why it wants the access, and the reports did not detail which routes Bagdogra flights would use, but eastern Nepal lies directly west of the airport, so access could allow more direct paths for international flights.

Nepal's tourism and civil aviation minister was due to travel to India on Tuesday, according to one report. Neither government had published a schedule for Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit to New Delhi; reports said it could take place between 22 and 25 November, and that the air routes are expected to be on the agenda. No public statement on the talks from India's Ministry of External Affairs or Ministry of Civil Aviation could be found.
